In this sample, the strategy underperformed Buy & Hold on both return and drawdown dimensions. The return gap is consistent with lower market participation: average exposure was 60.0%, while reduced exposure coincided with approximately 168.3 percentage points of uncaptured positive market return versus 136.8 points of downside cushion on an arithmetic attribution basis. This suggests the panic-side accumulation rule may be more useful than treating greed as a symmetric exit trigger in this sample. The next diagnostic step is to test drawdown attribution, market-regime performance, threshold sensitivity, and risk-adjusted metrics.

rows.answer: On 2023-06-16 QQQ's Panic Index was 9.37 (percentile 0.2), deep in the greed regime below the 15 sell threshold, built from VIX 13.54 and a Fear & Greed reading of 81.26 (extreme greed). In the greed regime the rule removes 10% from exposure each day, which is what it did on the latest observation: it now holds 0% at the floor. From that floor it would add only if the Panic Index closes above 64 into the panic regime, adding 20% per such day, and it has no room to reduce further below 0%. So the next meaningful trigger is a panic-regime move, not more calm. For context, Buy & Hold outperformed this rule over the standard window, returning 14.83% versus 5.73%.
